To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the t(9;6)(p24;q22) fusion gene in ACCs results in chimeric MYB-NFIF transcripts that encode a truncated MYB protein lacking the 3′ UTR, which includes target sites for the microRNAs miR-15/16 and mi-150, and that the fusion gene is a hallmark of the ACC and a candidate therapeutic target.
we have found a new mechanism of MYB activation in cancer involving MYB-NFIF gene fusion.
MYB-NF1 fusion transcripts are a recurrent genetic alteration in ACC of the breast and the head and neck.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the fusion partner gene of MYB in ACC.
identifying and characterizing new molecular alterations associated with the initiation and progression of cancer.
the identification of novel fusion oncogenes and the development of targeted therapy for human cancers with MYB activation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MYB gene is a bona fide oncogene that is activated by gene fusions in ACC and by gene duplication in some leukemias.
the MYB gene is involved in human carcinomas and that MYB-NF1B fusions are a hallmark of ACC.
the MYB fusion is a hallmark for ACC and that deregulated expression of MYB is an oncogenic event in ACC pathogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MYB is a new oncogene that is activated in ACC by fusion with NFIB and that this fusion is a hallmark for the ACC.
we have discovered a novel mechanism of MYB activation in human cancer involving the formation of chimeric transcripts.
the MYB gene is activated in human cancer by several distinct mechanisms, including amplification/duplication, translocation/fusion, and overexpression.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MYB gene can be activated by a variety of mechanisms, including translocation, duplication, and gene fusion, and that these mechanisms may have a common consequence of deregulating the expression of MYBF and its target genes.
we discovered a new oncogenic mechanism involving MYB gene fusions in human cancers.
we have identified a novel mechanism of MYB activation in human cancer involving the formation of a fusion gene.
